verses.modern: he went down to the secretary's room in the royal palace, where all the officials were sitting: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.

verses.kjv: Then Michaiah declared unto them all the words that he had heard, when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people.
verses.modern: Micaiah told them everything He had heard Baruch read to the people from the scroll.

verses.kjv: Therefore all the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, unto Baruch, saying, Take in thine hand the roll wherein thou hast read in the ears of the people, and come. So Baruch the son of Neriah took the roll in his hand, and came unto them.
verses.modern: Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to say to Baruch, "Bring the scroll from which You have been reading to the people and come." So Baruch son of Neriah went to them with the scroll in His hand.

verses.kjv: And they said unto him, Sit down now, and read it in our ears. So Baruch read it in their ears.
verses.modern: They said to Him, "Sit down, please, and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass, when they had heard all the words, they were afraid both one and other, and said unto Baruch, We will surely tell the king of all these words.
verses.modern: When they heard all these words, they looked at each other in fear and said to Baruch, "We must report all these words to the king."

verses.kjv: And they asked Baruch, saying, Tell us now, How didst thou write all these words at his mouth?
verses.modern: Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you come to write all this? Did Jeremiah dictate it?"

verses.kjv: Then Baruch answered them, He pronounced all these words unto me with his mouth, and I wrote them with ink in the book.
verses.modern: "Yes," Baruch replied, "he dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll."

verses.kjv: Then said the princes unto Baruch, Go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; and let no man know where ye be.
verses.modern: Then the officials said to Baruch, "You and Jeremiah must go and hide. Don't let anyone know where you are."

verses.kjv: And they went in to the king into the court, but they laid up the roll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and told all the words in the ears of the king.
verses.modern: After they put the scroll in the room of Elishama the secretary, they went to the king in the courtyard and reported everything to him.

verses.kjv: So the king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll: and he took it out of Elishama the scribe's chamber. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes which stood beside the king.
verses.modern: The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and Jehudi brought it from the room of Elishama the secretary and read it to the king and all the officials standing beside him.

verses.kjv: Now the king sat in the winterhouse in the ninth month: and there was a fire on the hearth burning before him.
verses.modern: It was the ninth month and the king was sitting in the winter apartment, with a fire burning in the firepot in front of him.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.
verses.modern: Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns of the scroll, the king cut them off with a scribe's knife and threw them into the firepot, until the entire scroll was burned in the fire.

verses.kjv: Yet they were not afraid, nor rent their garments, neither the king, nor any of his servants that heard all these words.
verses.modern: The king and all his attendants who heard all these words showed no fear, nor did they tear their clothes.

verses.kjv: Nevertheless Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the roll: but he would not hear them.
verses.modern: Even though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.

verses.kjv: But the king commanded Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to take Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet: but the LORD hid them.
verses.modern: Instead, the king commanded Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD had hidden them.

verses.kjv: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, after that the king had burned the roll, and the words which Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
verses.modern: After the king burned the scroll containing the words that Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

verses.kjv: Take thee again another roll, and write in it all the former words that were in the first roll, which Jehoiakim the king of Judah hath burned.
verses.modern: "Take another scroll and write on it all the words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned up.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, Thus saith the LORD; Thou hast burned this roll, saying, Why hast thou written therein, saying, The king of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land, and shall cause to cease from thence man and beast?
verses.modern: Also tell Jehoiakim king of Judah, 'This is what the LORD says: You burned that scroll and said, "Why did You write on it that the king of Babylon would certainly come and destroy this land and cut off both people and animals from it?"

verses.kjv: Therefore thus saith the LORD of Jehoiakim king of Judah; He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David: and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost.
verses.modern: Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David. His body will be thrown out and exposed to the heat by day and the frost by night.

verses.kjv: And I will punish him and his seed and his servants for their iniquity; and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them; but they hearkened not.
verses.modern: I will punish Him and His children and His attendants for their wickedness. I will bring on them and those living in Jerusalem and the people of Judah every disaster I pronounced against them, because they have not listened.'"

verses.kjv: Then took Jeremiah another roll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah; who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire: and there were added besides unto them many like words.
verses.modern: So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to the scribe Baruch son of Neriah. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on it all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.

chapters.summary: The LORD commanded Jeremiah to write all His words on a scroll. Baruch the scribe wrote at Jeremiah's dictation and read the scroll in the temple. King Jehoiakim had the scroll brought to him and cut it with a knife, piece by piece, and burned it in the fire. The LORD commanded Jeremiah to write another scroll, adding many similar words, and declared that Jehoiakim's dead body would be cast out.

verses.kjv: And king Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
verses.modern: Zedekiah son of Josiah was made king of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He reigned in place of Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim.

verses.kjv: But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, did hearken unto the words of the LORD, which he spake by the prophet Jeremiah.
verses.modern: Neither He nor His attendants nor the people of the land paid any attention to the words the LORD had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.

verses.kjv: And Zedekiah the king sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest to the prophet Jeremiah, saying, Pray now unto the LORD our God for us.
verses.modern: King Zedekiah, however, sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah with the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to ask Jeremiah the prophet, "Please pray to the LORD our God for us."

verses.kjv: Now Jeremiah came in and went out among the people: for they had not put him into prison.
verses.modern: Now Jeremiah was free to come and go among the people, for he had not yet been put in prison.

verses.kjv: Then Pharaoh's army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans that besieged Jerusalem heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem.
verses.modern: Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt, and when the Babylonians who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report about them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then came the word of the LORD unto the prophet Jeremiah, saying,
verses.modern: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel; Thus shall ye say to the king of Judah, that sent you unto me to enquire of me; Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land.
verses.modern: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Me: 'Pharaoh's army, which has marched out to support you, will go back to its own land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And the Chaldeans shall come again, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire.
verses.modern: Then the Babylonians will return and attack this city. They will capture it and burn it down.'

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD; Deceive not yourselves, saying, The Chaldeans shall surely depart from us: for they shall not depart.
verses.modern: "This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, thinking, 'The Babylonians will surely leave us.' They will not!

verses.kjv: For though ye had smitten the whole army of the Chaldeans that fight against you, and there remained but wounded men among them, yet should they rise up every man in his tent, and burn this city with fire.
verses.modern: Even if You were to defeat the entire Babylonian army that is attacking You and only wounded men were left in their tents, they would still rise up and burn this city down."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when the army of the Chaldeans was broken up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army,
verses.modern: After the Babylonian army had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,

verses.kjv: Then Jeremiah went forth out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to separate himself thence in the midst of the people.
verses.modern: Jeremiah started to leave the city to go to the territory of Benjamin to get his share of the property among the people there.

verses.kjv: And when he was in the gate of Benjamin, a captain of the ward was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he took Jeremiah the prophet, saying, Thou fallest away to the Chaldeans.
verses.modern: But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, the captain of the guard, whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah, arrested him and said, "You are deserting to the Babylonians!"

verses.kjv: Then said Jeremiah, It is false; I fall not away to the Chaldeans. But he hearkened not to him: so Irijah took Jeremiah, and brought him to the princes.
verses.modern: "That's not true!" Jeremiah said. "I am not deserting to the Babylonians." But Irijah would not listen to him. Instead, he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.

verses.kjv: Wherefore the princes were wroth with Jeremiah, and smote him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison.
verses.modern: They were angry with Jeremiah and had him beaten and imprisoned in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which they had made into a prison.

verses.kjv: When Jeremiah was entered into the dungeon, and into the cabins, and Jeremiah had remained there many days;
verses.modern: Jeremiah was put into a vaulted cell in a dungeon, where he remained a long time.

verses.kjv: Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took him out: and the king asked him secretly in his house, and said, Is there any word from the LORD? And Jeremiah said, There is: for, said he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.
verses.modern: Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where He asked Him privately, "Is there any word from the LORD?" "Yes," Jeremiah replied, "you will be given into the hands of the king of Babylon."

verses.kjv: Moreover Jeremiah said unto king Zedekiah, What have I offended against thee, or against thy servants, or against this people, that ye have put me in prison?
verses.modern: Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What crime have I committed against you, Your attendants, or this people, that You have put me in prison?

verses.kjv: Where are now your prophets which prophesied unto you, saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against you, nor against this land?
verses.modern: Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, 'The king of Babylon will not attack you or this land'?

verses.kjv: Therefore hear now, I pray thee, O my lord the king: let my supplication, I pray thee, be accepted before thee; that thou cause me not to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.
verses.modern: But now, my lord the king, please listen. Let my petition come before you. Please do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there."

verses.kjv: Then Zedekiah the king commanded that they should commit Jeremiah into the court of the prison, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread out of the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city were spent. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
verses.modern: King Zedekiah then gave orders for Jeremiah to be placed in the courtyard of the guard and given bread from the street of the bakers each day until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

chapters.summary: King Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah asking him to pray for the nation. Jeremiah warned that the Chaldeans would return and burn the city. When Jeremiah tried to leave Jerusalem, he was arrested as a deserter and thrown into a dungeon. Zedekiah secretly brought him out and asked for a word from the LORD, and Jeremiah told him he would be delivered into the king of Babylon's hand.

verses.kjv: Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people, saying,
verses.modern: Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jehukal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malkijah heard what Jeremiah had been telling all the people:

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, He that remaineth in this city shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: but he that goeth forth to the Chaldeans shall live; for he shall have his life for a prey, and shall live.
verses.modern: "This is what the LORD says: 'Whoever stays in this city will die by sword, famine, or plague. But whoever goes over to the Babylonians will live. They will escape with their lives.'

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, This city shall surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, which shall take it.
verses.modern: This is what the LORD says: 'This city will certainly be given into the hands of the army of the king of Babylon, who will capture it.'"

verses.kjv: Therefore the princes said unto the king, We beseech thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war that remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words unto them: for this man seeketh not the welfare of this people, but the hurt.
verses.modern: Then the officials said to the king, "This man should be put to death. He is discouraging the soldiers who are left in this city, as well as all the people, by the things he is saying. He is not seeking the good of these people but their ruin."

verses.kjv: Then Zedekiah the king said, Behold, he is in your hand: for the king is not he that can do any thing against you.
verses.modern: "He is in your hands," King Zedekiah answered. "The king can do nothing to oppose you."

verses.kjv: Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire.
verses.modern: So they took Jeremiah and put him into the cistern of Malkijah, the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah by ropes into the cistern. There was no water in it, only mud, and Jeremiah sank down into the mud.

verses.kjv: Now when Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon; the king then sitting in the gate of Benjamin;
verses.modern: Now when Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon — the king was sitting in the gate of Benjamin —

verses.kjv: Ebed-melech went forth out of the king's house, and spake to the king, saying,
verses.modern: Ebed-Melech went out of the palace and said to him:

verses.kjv: My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have cast into the dungeon; and he is like to die for hunger in the place where he is: for there is no more bread in the city.
verses.modern: "My lord the king, these men have acted wickedly in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into a cistern, where he will starve to death when there is no longer any bread in the city."

verses.kjv: Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.
verses.modern: Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, "Take thirty men with you from here and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon before he dies."

verses.kjv: So Ebed-melech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.
verses.modern: So Ebed-Melech took the men with him and went to a room under the treasury in the palace. He took some old rags and worn-out clothes from there and lowered them by ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.

verses.kjv: And Ebed-melech the Ethiopian said unto Jeremiah, Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords. And Jeremiah did so.
verses.modern: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah, "Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under your armpits under the cords." And Jeremiah did so,

verses.kjv: So they drew up Jeremiah with cords, and took him up out of the dungeon: and Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
verses.modern: and they pulled him up with the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

verses.kjv: Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took Jeremiah the prophet unto him into the third entry that is in the house of the LORD: and the king said unto Jeremiah, I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me.
verses.modern: Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to the third entrance to the temple of the LORD. "I am going to ask You something," the king said to Jeremiah. "Do not hide anything from me."

verses.kjv: Then Jeremiah said unto Zedekiah, If I declare it unto thee, wilt thou not surely put me to death? and if I give thee counsel, wilt thou not hearken unto me?
verses.modern: Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I give you an answer, will you not kill me? Even if I do give you counsel, you will not listen to me."

verses.kjv: So Zedekiah the king sware secretly unto Jeremiah, saying, As the LORD liveth, that made us this soul, I will not put thee to death, neither will I give thee into the hand of these men that seek thy life.
verses.modern: But King Zedekiah swore this oath secretly to Jeremiah: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has given us breath, I will neither kill You nor hand You over to those who want to kill You."

verses.kjv: Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house:
verses.modern: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'If you surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared and this city will not be burned down. You and Your family will live.

verses.kjv: But if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylon's princes, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.
verses.modern: But if you will not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city will be given into the hands of the Babylonians and they will burn it down. You yourself will not escape from their hands.'"

verses.kjv: And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me.
verses.modern: King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have already gone over to the Babylonians. The Babylonians may hand me over to them and they will abuse me."

verses.kjv: But Jeremiah said, They shall not deliver thee. Obey, I beseech thee, the voice of the LORD, which I speak unto thee: so it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.
verses.modern: "They will not hand You over," Jeremiah replied. "Obey the LORD by doing what I tell You. Then it will go well with You and Your life will be spared.

verses.kjv: But if thou refuse to go forth, this is the word that the LORD hath shewed me:
verses.modern: But if You refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has revealed to me:

verses.kjv: And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah's house shall be brought forth to the king of Babylon's princes, and those women shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back.
verses.modern: All the women left in the palace of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon. Those women will say to you: 'They misled you and overcame you — your trusted friends. Now that your feet are sunk in the mud, your friends have turned away.'

verses.kjv: So they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.
verses.modern: All your wives and children will be brought out to the Babylonians. You yourself will not escape from their hands but will be captured by the king of Babylon. And this city will be burned down."

verses.kjv: Then said Zedekiah unto Jeremiah, Let no man know of these words, and thou shalt not die.
verses.modern: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not let anyone know about this conversation, or you may die.

verses.kjv: But if the princes hear that I have talked with thee, and they come unto thee, and say unto thee, Declare unto us now what thou hast said unto the king, hide it not from us, and we will not put thee to death; also what the king said unto thee:
verses.modern: If the officials hear that I talked with you, and they come to you and say, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you — do not hide it from us or we will kill you' —

verses.kjv: Then thou shalt say unto them, I presented my supplication before the king, that he would not cause me to return to Jonathan's house, to die there.
verses.modern: then tell them, 'I was pleading with the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"

verses.kjv: Then came all the princes unto Jeremiah, and asked him: and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded. So they left off speaking with him; for the matter was not perceived.
verses.modern: All the officials did come to Jeremiah and question him, and he told them everything the king had ordered him to say. So they said no more to him, for no one had heard his conversation with the king.

verses.kjv: So Jeremiah abode in the court of the prison until the day that Jerusalem was taken: and he was there when Jerusalem was taken.
verses.modern: And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.

chapters.summary: The princes cast Jeremiah into a muddy cistern to die because his words discouraged the soldiers. Ebedmelech the Ethiopian persuaded the king to rescue him, and Jeremiah was pulled out with ropes and rags. Zedekiah secretly consulted Jeremiah, who told him that if he surrendered to Babylon the city would not be burned and he would live, but Zedekiah feared the Jews who had already defected.

verses.kjv: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, came Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army against Jerusalem, and they besieged it.
verses.modern: This is how Jerusalem was captured: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army and laid siege to it.

verses.kjv: And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, the city was broken up.
verses.modern: And on the ninth day of the fourth month of Zedekiah's eleventh year, the city wall was broken through.

verses.kjv: And all the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even Nergalsharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon.
verses.modern: Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came and took seats in the Middle Gate: Nergal-Sharezer of Samgar, Nebo-Sarsekim a chief officer, Nergal-Sharezer a high official, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night, by the way of the king's garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain.
verses.modern: When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled. They left the city at night by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Arabah.

verses.kjv: But the Chaldeans' army pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him.
verses.modern: But the Babylonian army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and took him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced sentence on him.

verses.kjv: Then the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes: also the king of Babylon slew all the nobles of Judah.
verses.modern: There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes. The king of Babylon also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.

verses.kjv: Moreover he put out Zedekiah's eyes, and bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon.
verses.modern: Then he gouged out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him with bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.

verses.kjv: And the Chaldeans burned the king's house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.modern: The Babylonians set fire to the royal palace and the houses of the people. They broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive into Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to him, with the rest of the people that remained.
verses.modern: Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard carried into exile to Babylon the people who remained in the city, along with those who had gone over to him and the rest of the people.

verses.kjv: But Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
verses.modern: But Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard left behind in the land of Judah some of the poor people, who owned nothing. At that time he gave them vineyards and fields.

verses.kjv: Now Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave charge concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard, saying,
verses.modern: Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given these orders about Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard:

verses.kjv: Take him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do unto him even as he shall say unto thee.
verses.modern: "Take him and look after him. Don't harm him but do for him whatever he asks."

verses.kjv: So Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard sent, and Nebushasban, Rabsaris, and Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, and all the king of Babylon's princes;
verses.modern: So Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard, Nebushazban a chief officer, Nergal-Sharezer a high official, and all the other officers of the king of Babylon

verses.kjv: Even they sent, and took Jeremiah out of the court of the prison, and committed him unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, that he should carry him home: so he dwelt among the people.
verses.modern: sent and had Jeremiah taken out of the courtyard of the guard. They turned him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to take him back to his home. So he remained among his own people.

verses.kjv: Now the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah, while he was shut up in the court of the prison, saying,
verses.modern: While Jeremiah had been confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD had come to Him:

verses.kjv: Go and speak to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.
verses.modern: "Go and speak to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: I will bring My words upon this city for evil and not for good. They shall be accomplished before You in that day.

verses.kjv: But I will deliver thee in that day, saith the LORD: and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid.
verses.modern: But I will rescue You on that day,' says the LORD. 'You will not be given into the hands of those You fear.

verses.kjv: For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the LORD.
verses.modern: I will save You. You will not fall by the sword but will escape with Your life, because You trust in Me,' says the LORD."

chapters.summary: Nebuchadnezzar's army broke through the walls of Jerusalem in the eleventh year of Zedekiah. Zedekiah fled but was captured near Jericho; his sons were killed before his eyes, then his eyes were put out and he was bound in chains for Babylon. Nebuzaradan burned the city but released Jeremiah and commanded that he be treated well. The LORD promised Ebedmelech that his life would be spared.

verses.kjv: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, after that Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all that were carried away captive of Jerusalem and Judah, which were carried away captive unto Babylon.
verses.modern: The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard had released Him at Ramah. He had found Jeremiah bound in chains among all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried into exile to Babylon.

verses.kjv: And the captain of the guard took Jeremiah, and said unto him, The LORD thy God hath pronounced this evil upon this place.
verses.modern: When the commander of the guard found Jeremiah, he said to him: "The LORD Your God decreed this disaster for this place.

verses.kjv: Now the LORD hath brought it, and done according as he hath said: because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you.
verses.modern: And the LORD has brought it about. He has done just as He said He would. All this happened because You people sinned against the LORD and did not obey Him.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, I loose thee this day from the chains which were upon thine hand. If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look well unto thee: but if it seem ill unto thee to come with me into Babylon, forbear: behold, all the land is before thee: whither it seemeth good and convenient for thee to go, thither go.
verses.modern: But today I am freeing You from the chains on Your wrists. Come with me to Babylon, if You like, and I will look after You. But if You do not want to come, then don't. See, the whole land lies before You. Go wherever You please."

verses.kjv: Now while he was not yet gone back, he said, Go back also to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon hath made governor over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him among the people: or go wheresoever it seemeth convenient unto thee to go. So the captain of the guard gave him victuals and a reward, and let him go.
verses.modern: But before Jeremiah turned to go, Nebuzaradan added, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the towns of Judah, and live with him among the people, or go anywhere else you please." Then the commander gave him provisions and a present and let him go.

verses.kjv: So Jeremiah went unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and dwelt with him among the people that were left in the land.
verses.modern: So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with Him among the people who were left behind in the land.

verses.kjv: Now when all the captains of the forces which were in the fields, even they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed unto him men, and women, and children, and of the poor of the land, of them that were not carried away captive to Babylon;
verses.modern: When all the army officers and their men who were still in the open country heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam as governor over the land and had put him in charge of the men, women, and children who were the poorest in the land and had not been carried into exile to Babylon,

verses.kjv: Then they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.
verses.modern: they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah — Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maakathite, and their men.

verses.kjv: And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan sware unto them and to their men, saying, Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.
verses.modern: Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, took an oath to reassure them and their men. "Do not be afraid to serve the Babylonians," he said. "Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

verses.kjv: As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah, to serve the Chaldeans, which will come unto us: but ye, gather ye wine, and summer fruits, and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that ye have taken.
verses.modern: I myself will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Babylonians who come to us. You are to harvest the wine, summer fruit, and olive oil, and put them in your storage jars. Live in the towns you have taken over."

verses.kjv: Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan;
verses.modern: When all the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and all the other countries heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, over them,

verses.kjv: Then they returned out of all places whither they were driven, even Judah, to Gedaliah, unto Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruits very much.
verses.modern: they all came back to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, from all the countries where they had been scattered. And they harvested an abundance of wine and summer fruit.

verses.kjv: Moreover Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were in the fields, came to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
verses.modern: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers still in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah

verses.kjv: And said unto him, Dost thou certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites hath sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee? But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not.
verses.modern: and said to him, "Don't you know that Baalis king of Ammon has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

verses.kjv: Then Johanan the son of Kareah spake to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it: wherefore should he slay thee, that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?
verses.modern: Then Johanan son of Kareah said privately to Gedaliah in Mizpah, "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know it. Why should he take your life and cause all the Jews who have gathered around you to be scattered, and the remnant of Judah to perish?"

verses.kjv: But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said unto Johanan the son of Kareah, Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.
verses.modern: But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Don't do such a thing! What you are saying about Ishmael is not true."

chapters.summary: Nebuzaradan released Jeremiah at Ramah and gave him the choice to go to Babylon or stay. Jeremiah chose to stay with Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor over the remnant in Judah. Gedaliah gathered the scattered people and told them to serve the Chaldeans and it would be well with them, but Johanan warned Gedaliah that Ishmael planned to murder him.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, and the princes of the king, even ten men with him, came unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there they did eat bread together in Mizpah.
verses.modern: In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was of royal blood and had been one of the king's officers, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. While they were eating together there,

verses.kjv: Then arose Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men that were with him, and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
verses.modern: Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him rose up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with the sword, killing the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed as governor over the land.

verses.kjv: Ishmael also slew all the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war.
verses.modern: Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, as well as the Babylonian soldiers who were there.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass the second day after he had slain Gedaliah, and no man knew it,
verses.modern: The day after Gedaliah's assassination, before anyone knew about it,

verses.kjv: That there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the LORD.
verses.modern: eighty men who had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They were bringing grain offerings and incense to the house of the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and it came to pass, as he met them, he said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.
verses.modern: Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as He went. When He met them, He said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."

verses.kjv: And it was so, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the midst of the pit, he, and the men that were with him.
verses.modern: When they came into the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men with Him slaughtered them and threw them into a cistern.

verses.kjv: But ten men were found among them that said unto Ishmael, Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey. So he forbare, and slew them not among their brethren.
verses.modern: But ten of them said to Ishmael, "Don't kill us! We have wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey hidden in a field." So He let them alone and did not kill them with the others.

verses.kjv: Now the pit wherein Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah, was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with them that were slain.
verses.modern: Now the cistern where he threw all the bodies of the men he had killed was the large cistern that King Asa had made as part of his defense against Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the dead.

verses.kjv: Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king's daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the children of Ammon.
verses.modern: Ishmael made captives of all the rest of the people who were in Mizpah — the king's daughters along with all the others who were left there, over whom Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to Ammon.

verses.kjv: But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,
verses.modern: When Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers with him heard about all the crimes Ishmael son of Nethaniah had committed,

verses.kjv: Then they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and found him by the great waters that are in Gibeon.
verses.modern: they took all their men and went to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They caught up with him near the great pool in Gibeon.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass, that when all the people which were with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, then they were glad.
verses.modern: When all the people Ishmael had with him saw Johanan son of Kareah and the army officers with him, they were glad.

verses.kjv: So all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah cast about and returned, and went unto Johanan the son of Kareah.
verses.modern: All the people Ishmael had taken captive at Mizpah turned around and came over to Johanan son of Kareah.

verses.kjv: But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the children of Ammon.
verses.modern: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah and eight of his men escaped from Johanan and fled to Ammon.

verses.kjv: Then took Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after that he had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam; even mighty men of war, and the women, and the children, and the eunuchs, whom he had brought again from Gibeon:
verses.modern: Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers with him led away all the survivors from Mizpah who had been recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah after he had assassinated Gedaliah son of Ahikam — the soldiers, women, children, and court officials he had brought from Gibeon.

verses.kjv: And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem, to go to enter into Egypt,
verses.modern: And they went on, stopping at Geruth Kimham near Bethlehem on their way to Egypt

verses.kjv: Because of the Chaldeans: for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor in the land.
verses.modern: to escape from the Babylonians. They were afraid of them because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed as governor over the land.

chapters.summary: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal family, came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and murdered him along with the Jews and Chaldean soldiers who were with him. He killed seventy of eighty men who came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, and took the remnant captive. Johanan and his forces pursued Ishmael and rescued the captives, but Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites.

verses.kjv: Then all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest, came near,
verses.modern: Then all the army officers, including Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest approached

verses.kjv: And said unto Jeremiah the prophet, Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee, and pray for us unto the LORD thy God, even for all this remnant; (for we are left but a few of many, as thine eyes do behold us:)
verses.modern: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Please hear our petition and pray to the LORD your God for this entire remnant. For as you now see, though we were once many, now only a few are left.

verses.kjv: That the LORD thy God may shew us the way wherein we may walk, and the thing that we may do.
verses.modern: Pray that the LORD Your God will tell us where we should go and what we should do."

verses.kjv: Then Jeremiah the prophet said unto them, I have heard you; behold, I will pray unto the LORD your God according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatsoever thing the LORD shall answer you, I will declare it unto you; I will keep nothing back from you.
verses.modern: "I have heard You," replied Jeremiah the prophet. "I will certainly pray to the LORD Your God as You have requested. I will tell You everything the LORD says and will keep nothing back from You."

verses.kjv: Then they said to Jeremiah, The LORD be a true and faithful witness between us, if we do not even according to all things for the which the LORD thy God shall send thee to us.
verses.modern: Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act in accordance with everything the LORD Your God sends You to tell us.

verses.kjv: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.
verses.modern: Whether it is favorable or unfavorable, we will obey the LORD our God, to whom we are sending You, so that it will go well with us, for we will obey the LORD our God."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after ten days, that the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah.
verses.modern: Ten days later the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.

verses.kjv: Then called he Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces which were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
verses.modern: So He called together Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers who were with Him and all the people from the least to the greatest.

verses.kjv: And said unto them, Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, unto whom ye sent me to present your supplication before him:
verses.modern: He said to them: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom You sent me to present Your petition, says:

verses.kjv: If ye will still abide in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up: for I repent me of the evil that I have done unto you.
verses.modern: 'If You stay in this land, I will build You up and not tear You down. I will plant You and not uproot You, for I am grieved over the disaster I have inflicted on You.

verses.kjv: Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom ye are afraid; be not afraid of him, saith the LORD: for I am with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.
verses.modern: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear. Do not be afraid of Him,' says the LORD, 'for I am with You and will save You and deliver You from His hands.

verses.kjv: And I will shew mercies unto you, that he may have mercy upon you, and cause you to return to your own land.
verses.modern: I will show You compassion so that He will have compassion on You and restore You to Your land.'

verses.kjv: But if ye say, We will not dwell in this land, neither obey the voice of the LORD your God,
verses.modern: But if You say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the LORD Your God,

verses.kjv: Saying, No, but we will go into the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell:
verses.modern: and if You say, 'No, we will go and live in Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the trumpet or be hungry for bread,'

verses.kjv: And now therefore hear the word of the LORD, ye remnant of Judah; Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; If ye wholly set your faces to enter into Egypt, and go to sojourn there;
verses.modern: then hear the word of the LORD, You remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'If You are determined to go to Egypt and You do go to settle there,

verses.kjv: Then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die.
verses.modern: then the sword You fear will overtake You there, and the famine You dread will follow You into Egypt, and there You will die.

verses.kjv: So shall it be with all the men that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: and none of them shall remain or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them.
verses.modern: Indeed, all who are determined to go to Egypt to settle there will die by sword, famine, and plague. Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I will bring on them.'

verses.kjv: For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; As mine anger and my fury hath been poured forth upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem; so shall my fury be poured forth upon you, when ye shall enter into Egypt: and ye shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach; and ye shall see this place no more.
verses.modern: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'Just as My anger and wrath have been poured out on those who lived in Jerusalem, so will My wrath be poured out on You when You go to Egypt. You will be a curse and an object of horror, a curse and a disgrace. You will never see this place again.'

verses.kjv: The LORD hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day.
verses.modern: The LORD has told You, You remnant of Judah, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Be sure of this: I warn You today

verses.kjv: For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the LORD your God, saying, Pray for us unto the LORD our God; and according unto all that the LORD our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it.
verses.modern: that You made a fatal mistake when You sent me to the LORD Your God and said, 'Pray to the LORD our God for us. Tell us everything He says and we will do it.'

verses.kjv: And now I have this day declared it to you; but ye have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God, nor any thing for the which he hath sent me unto you.
verses.modern: I have told You today, but You still have not obeyed the LORD Your God in all He sent me to tell You.

verses.kjv: Now therefore know certainly that ye shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, in the place whither ye desire to go and to sojourn.
verses.modern: So now, be sure of this: You will die by sword, famine, and plague in the place where You want to go and settle."

chapters.summary: Johanan and the remnant asked Jeremiah to pray and inquire of the LORD whether they should stay in Judah or go to Egypt, swearing to obey whatever the LORD said. After ten days the LORD answered: if they stayed in the land He would build them up and plant them, but if they went to Egypt the sword and famine they feared would follow them there, and they would die.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking unto all the people all the words of the LORD their God, for which the LORD their God had sent him to them, even all these words,
verses.modern: When Jeremiah finished telling the people all the words of the LORD their God — everything the LORD had sent Him to tell them —

verses.kjv: Then spake Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men, saying unto Jeremiah, Thou speakest falsely: the LORD our God hath not sent thee to say, Go not into Egypt to sojourn there:
verses.modern: Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God has not sent you to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to settle there.'

verses.kjv: But Baruch the son of Neriah setteth thee on against us, for to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they might put us to death, and carry us away captives into Babylon.
verses.modern: But Baruch son of Neriah is inciting You against us to hand us over to the Babylonians, so they may kill us or carry us into exile to Babylon."

verses.kjv: So Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, and all the people, obeyed not the voice of the LORD, to dwell in the land of Judah.
verses.modern: So Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers and all the people disobeyed the LORD's command to stay in the land of Judah.

verses.kjv: But Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, took all the remnant of Judah, that were returned from all nations, whither they had been driven, to dwell in the land of Judah;
verses.modern: Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers led away all the remnant of Judah who had come back to live in the land of Judah from all the nations where they had been scattered.

verses.kjv: Even men, and women, and children, and the king's daughters, and every person that Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah.
verses.modern: They included men, women, and children, the king's daughters, and everyone Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan — and also Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.

verses.kjv: So they came into the land of Egypt: for they obeyed not the voice of the LORD: thus came they even to Tahpanhes.
verses.modern: So they entered Egypt in disobedience to the LORD and went as far as Tahpanhes.

verses.kjv: Then came the word of the LORD unto Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.modern: In Tahpanhes the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

verses.kjv: Take great stones in thine hand, and hide them in the clay in the brickwork, which is at the entry of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah;
verses.modern: "While the Jews are watching, take some large stones with you and bury them in clay in the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes.

verses.kjv: And say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid; and he shall spread his royal pavilion over them.
verses.modern: Then say to them, 'This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and I will set his throne over these stones I have buried here. He will spread His royal canopy above them.

verses.kjv: And when he cometh, he shall smite the land of Egypt, and deliver such as are for death to death; and such as are for captivity to captivity; and such as are for the sword to the sword.
verses.modern: He will come and attack Egypt, bringing death to those destined for death, captivity to those destined for captivity, and the sword to those destined for the sword.

verses.kjv: And I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt; and he shall burn them, and carry them away captives: and he shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd putteth on his garment; and he shall go forth from thence in peace.
verses.modern: He will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt. He will burn their temples and take their gods captive. As a shepherd wraps His garment around Him, so He will wrap Egypt around Himself and depart from there unharmed.

verses.kjv: He shall break also the images of Bethshemesh, that is in the land of Egypt; and the houses of the gods of Egypt shall he burn with fire.
verses.modern: There in the temple of the sun in Egypt He will demolish the sacred pillars and will burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt.'"

chapters.summary: Johanan and the proud men accused Jeremiah of lying and refused to obey the LORD's command to remain in Judah. They took the entire remnant, including Jeremiah and Baruch, and went down to Egypt. At Tahpanhes the LORD told Jeremiah to hide stones in the clay at the brickworks, for Nebuchadnezzar would set his throne over them and strike the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews which dwell in the land of Egypt, which dwell at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Noph, and in the country of Pathros, saying,
verses.modern: This word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in Lower Egypt — in Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis — and in Upper Egypt:

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Ye have seen all the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, and upon all the cities of Judah; and, behold, this day they are a desolation, and no man dwelleth therein,
verses.modern: "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You saw the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Today they lie deserted and in ruins

verses.kjv: Because of their wickedness which they have committed to provoke me to anger, in that they went to burn incense, and to serve other gods, whom they knew not, neither they, nor you, nor your fathers.
verses.modern: because of the evil they did to arouse My anger, in that they went to burn incense and to worship other gods that neither they nor You nor Your ancestors ever knew.

verses.kjv: Howbeit I sent unto you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate.
verses.modern: Again and again I sent My servants the prophets, who said, 'Do not do this detestable thing that I hate!'

verses.kjv: But they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness, to burn no incense unto other gods.
verses.modern: But they did not listen or pay attention. They did not turn from their wickedness or stop burning incense to other gods.

verses.kjv: Wherefore my fury and mine anger was poured forth, and was kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they are wasted and desolate, as at this day.
verses.modern: Therefore My fierce anger was poured out. It raged against the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem and made them the desolate ruins they are today.

verses.kjv: Therefore now thus saith the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; Wherefore commit ye this great evil against your souls, to cut off from you man and woman, child and suckling, out of Judah, to leave you none to remain;
verses.modern: "Now this is what the LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why bring such great disaster on yourselves by cutting off from Judah the men and women, the children and infants, and so leave yourselves without a remnant?

verses.kjv: In that ye provoke me unto wrath with the works of your hands, burning incense unto other gods in the land of Egypt, whither ye be gone to dwell, that ye might cut yourselves off, and that ye might be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
verses.modern: Why arouse My anger with what Your hands have made, burning incense to other gods in Egypt, where You have come to live? You will destroy yourselves and make yourselves a curse and a disgrace among all the nations on earth.

verses.kjv: Have ye forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, and the wickedness of the kings of Judah, and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives, which they have committed in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?
verses.modern: Have You forgotten the wickedness committed by Your ancestors and by the kings and queens of Judah and the wickedness committed by You and Your wives in the land of Judah and on the streets of Jerusalem?

verses.kjv: They are not humbled even unto this day, neither have they feared, nor walked in my law, nor in my statutes, that I set before you and before your fathers.
verses.modern: To this day they have not humbled themselves or shown reverence, nor have they followed My law and the decrees I set before You and Your ancestors.

verses.kjv: Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will set my face against you for evil, and to cut off all Judah.
verses.modern: Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am determined to bring disaster on You and to destroy all Judah.

verses.kjv: And I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they shall all be consumed, and fall in the land of Egypt; they shall even be consumed by the sword and by the famine: they shall die, from the least even unto the greatest, by the sword and by the famine: and they shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach.
verses.modern: I will take away the remnant of Judah who were determined to go to Egypt to settle there. They will all perish in Egypt. They will fall by the sword or die from famine. From the least to the greatest, they will die by sword or famine. They will become a curse and an object of horror, a curse and a disgrace.

verses.kjv: For I will punish them that dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence:
verses.modern: I will punish those who live in Egypt with sword, famine, and plague, just as I punished Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: So that none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah, to the which they have a desire to return to dwell there: for none shall return but such as shall escape.
verses.modern: None of the remnant of Judah who have gone to live in Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, to which they long to return and live. None will return except a few fugitives."

verses.kjv: Then all the men which knew that their wives had burned incense unto other gods, and all the women that stood by, a great congregation, even all the people that dwelt in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
verses.modern: Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, along with all the women who were present — a large assembly — and all the people living in Lower and Upper Egypt, said to Jeremiah:

verses.kjv: As for the word that thou hast spoken unto us in the name of the LORD, we will not hearken unto thee.
verses.modern: "We will not listen to the message You have spoken to us in the name of the LORD!

verses.kjv: But we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, as we have done, we, and our fathers, our kings, and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem: and then had we plenty of victuals, and were well, and saw no evil.
verses.modern: We will certainly carry out every word that has come from our own mouths. We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and will pour out drink offerings to her just as we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials did in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. At that time we had plenty of food and were well off and suffered no harm.

verses.kjv: But since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.
verses.modern: But ever since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have had nothing and have been perishing by sword and famine."

verses.kjv: And when we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured out drink offerings unto her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings unto her, without our men?
verses.modern: The women added, "When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes impressed with her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands knowing it?"

verses.kjv: Then Jeremiah said unto all the people, to the men, and to the women, and to all the people which had given him that answer, saying,
verses.modern: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, both men and women, who were answering him:

verses.kjv: The incense that ye burned in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, ye, and your fathers, your kings, and your princes, and the people of the land, did not the LORD remember them, and came it not into his mind?
verses.modern: "Did not the LORD remember and call to mind the incense burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem by You and Your ancestors, Your kings and Your officials and the people of the land?

verses.kjv: So that the LORD could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings, and because of the abominations which ye have committed; therefore is your land a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse, without an inhabitant, as at this day.
verses.modern: When the LORD could no longer endure Your wicked actions and the detestable things You did, Your land became a curse and a desolate waste without inhabitants, as it is today.

verses.kjv: Because ye have burned incense, and because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, nor walked in his law, nor in his statutes, nor in his testimonies; therefore this evil is happened unto you, as at this day.
verses.modern: This disaster came on You because You burned incense and sinned against the LORD and did not obey the LORD or follow His law, His decrees, or His stipulations. That is why this disaster has come upon You, as You now see."

verses.kjv: Moreover Jeremiah said unto all the people, and to all the women, Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah that are in the land of Egypt:
verses.modern: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, including the women, "Hear the word of the LORD, all You people of Judah in Egypt.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, saying; Ye and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hand, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her: ye will surely accomplish your vows, and surely perform your vows.
verses.modern: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You and Your wives have done what You said You would do when You promised, 'We will certainly carry out the vows we made to burn incense and pour out drink offerings to the Queen of Heaven.' Go ahead then, do what you promised! Keep Your vows!

verses.kjv: Therefore hear ye the word of the LORD, all Judah that dwell in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, saith the LORD, that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord GOD liveth.
verses.modern: But hear the word of the LORD, all Jews living in Egypt: 'I swear by My great name,' says the LORD, 'that no one from Judah living anywhere in Egypt will ever again invoke My name or swear, "As surely as the Lord GOD lives."

verses.kjv: Behold, I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them.
verses.modern: For I am watching over them for harm, not for good. The Jews in Egypt will perish by sword and famine until they are all destroyed.

verses.kjv: Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs.
verses.modern: Those who escape the sword and return to the land of Judah from Egypt will be very few. Then the whole remnant of Judah who came to live in Egypt will know whose word will stand — Mine or theirs.

verses.kjv: And this shall be a sign unto you, saith the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, that ye may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil:
verses.modern: This will be the sign to You that I will punish You in this place,' says the LORD, 'so that You will know that My threats of harm against You will surely come true':

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will give Pharaohhophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.
verses.modern: 'I am going to give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hands of his enemies who want to kill him, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the enemy who wanted to kill him.'"

chapters.summary: Jeremiah warned the Jews in Egypt that the LORD's anger had burned against Jerusalem because of their idolatry, and now they were provoking Him again by burning incense to the queen of heaven in Egypt. The people defiantly refused to listen, insisting they would continue their offerings to the queen of heaven. The LORD declared that the remnant in Egypt would be consumed by sword and famine.

verses.kjv: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spake unto Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
verses.modern: This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, after Baruch had written on a scroll the words Jeremiah dictated. He said:

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, unto thee, O Baruch;
verses.modern: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to You, Baruch:

verses.kjv: Thou didst say, Woe is me now! for the LORD hath added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest.
verses.modern: You said, 'Woe to me! The LORD has added sorrow to my pain. I am worn out with groaning and find no rest.'

verses.kjv: Thus shalt thou say unto him, The LORD saith thus; Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land.
verses.modern: But the LORD says: 'I will overthrow what I have built and uproot what I have planted — this entire land.

verses.kjv: And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD: but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest.
verses.modern: Should You then seek great things for Yourself? Do not seek them. For I will bring disaster on all people,' says the LORD, 'but wherever You go I will let You escape with Your life.'"

chapters.summary: The LORD gave Jeremiah a personal word for Baruch the scribe, who had complained of his sorrow and weariness. The LORD told Baruch that He was about to tear down what He had built and uproot what He had planted over the whole land. He warned Baruch not to seek great things for himself, but promised that his life would be given to him as a prize wherever he went.

verses.kjv: The word of the LORD which came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Gentiles;
verses.modern: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations:

verses.kjv: Against Egypt, against the army of Pharaohnecho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah:
verses.modern: Concerning Egypt: This is the message against the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, which was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:

verses.kjv: Order ye the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle.
verses.modern: "Prepare your shields, both large and small, and march out for battle!

verses.kjv: Harness the horses; and get up, ye horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, and put on the brigandines.
verses.modern: Harness the horses. Mount the steeds! Take your positions with helmets on! Polish your spears. Put on your armor!

verses.kjv: Wherefore have I seen them dismayed and turned away back? and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled apace, and look not back: for fear was round about, saith the LORD.
verses.modern: What do I see? They are terrified. They are retreating. Their warriors are defeated. They flee in haste without looking back — and there is terror on every side," says the LORD.

verses.kjv: Let not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; they shall stumble, and fall toward the north by the river Euphrates.
verses.modern: "The swift cannot flee nor the strong escape. In the north by the River Euphrates they stumble and fall.

verses.kjv: Who is this that cometh up as a flood, whose waters are moved as the rivers?
verses.modern: Who is this that rises like the Nile, like rivers of surging waters?

verses.kjv: Egypt riseth up like a flood, and his waters are moved like the rivers; and he saith, I will go up, and will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and the inhabitants thereof.
verses.modern: Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers of surging waters. She says, 'I will rise and cover the earth. I will destroy cities and their people.'

verses.kjv: Come up, ye horses; and rage, ye chariots; and let the mighty men come forth; the Ethiopians and the Libyans, that handle the shield; and the Lydians, that handle and bend the bow.
verses.modern: Come up, You horses! Rage, You chariots! Let the mighty men come forth — the Ethiopians and the Libyans who handle the shield, and the Lydians who handle and bend the bow.

verses.kjv: For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood: for the Lord GOD of hosts hath a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
verses.modern: But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of hosts — a day of vengeance, for vengeance on His foes. The sword will devour till it is satisfied, till it has quenched its thirst with blood. For the Lord GOD of hosts will offer sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.

verses.kjv: Go up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin, the daughter of Egypt: in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured.
verses.modern: "Go up to Gilead and get balm, Virgin Daughter Egypt. But You multiply remedies in vain. There is no healing for You.

verses.kjv: The nations have heard of thy shame, and thy cry hath filled the land: for the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty, and they are fallen both together.
verses.modern: The nations will hear of your shame. Your cries will fill the earth. One warrior will stumble over another. Both will fall down together."

verses.kjv: The word that the LORD spake to Jeremiah the prophet, how Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: This is the message the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to attack Egypt:

verses.kjv: Declare ye in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and publish in Noph and in Tahpanhes: say ye, Stand fast, and prepare thee; for the sword shall devour round about thee.
