verses.kjv: And a chapiter of brass was upon it; and the height of one chapiter was five cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the chapiter round about, all of brass. The second pillar also and the pomegranates were like unto these.
verses.modern: The bronze capital on top of one pillar was five cubits high and was decorated with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around. The other pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.

verses.kjv: And there were ninety and six pomegranates on a side; and all the pomegranates upon the network were an hundred round about.
verses.modern: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides. The total number of pomegranates above the surrounding network was one hundred.

verses.kjv: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:
verses.modern: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank, and the three doorkeepers.

verses.kjv: He took also out of the city an eunuch, which had the charge of the men of war; and seven men of them that were near the king's person, which were found in the city; and the principal scribe of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city.
verses.modern: Of those still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the fighting men and seven of the king's advisors. He also took the secretary who was chief officer in charge of conscripting the people of the land, and sixty of the common people who were found inside the city.

verses.kjv: So Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
verses.modern: Nebuzaradan the commander took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

verses.kjv: And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land.
verses.modern: There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king had them executed. So Judah went into exile, away from her land.

verses.kjv: This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty:
verses.modern: This is the number of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;

verses.kjv: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty and two persons:
verses.modern: in Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;

verses.kjv: In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar, Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred.
verses.modern: in his twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard took into exile 745 Jews. There were 4,600 people in all.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the first year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison.
verses.modern: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the year Awel-Marduk became king of Babylon, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, he released Jehoiachin king of Judah and freed him from prison.

verses.kjv: And spake kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon.
verses.modern: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

verses.kjv: And changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life.
verses.modern: So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king's table.

verses.kjv: And for his diet, there was a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
verses.modern: Day by day the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin a regular allowance as long as he lived, until the day of his death.

chapters.summary: Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, and in the fourth month the famine was severe. The city was broken up, Zedekiah was captured, and his sons were killed before his eyes. Nebuzaradan burned the temple, the palace, and every great house in Jerusalem, broke down the walls, and carried the people into exile. Jehoiachin was released from prison in Babylon and given a place at the king's table for the rest of his life.
